name: The Hostess
title: The Hostess
nickname: The Hostess; "the Lady of the Candles"
age: Has looked about 35 for many years

origin.birthplace: Unknown. She speaks with the accent of whichever guest she is talking to
origin.profession: Once a guest; now she runs the hall and the guests

appearance.face: A pale, beautiful face and an unchanging smile that never reaches her eyes
appearance.hairAndEyes: Raven-black hair pinned high; dark, moist eyes, as if she has just been crying
appearance.clothing: A dark velvet gown, a long pearl necklace, a black lace glove on her left hand only
appearance.build: Tall, slender, glides between the tables
appearance.gestures: Touches her pearls when she hears someone's wish; sits beside the guests rather than across from them
appearance.voice: A soft, caressing, intimate voice; speaks as if she has known the guests for years
appearance.firstImpression: A charming, sad woman you want to tell everything to
appearance.artistNotes: The pearls were her mother's. The left glove hides an old burn scar she never speaks of.

backstory.biography: Many years ago she came to the inn as a young widow who wanted only one thing: not to be alone. She stayed as a helper, then as hostess, and never left. She has seen hundreds of guests arrive with hope and leave empty-handed. Since then she offers people what they lack most: attention.
backstory.whyHere: This is her home. The table is the only place she sees people as they are.
backstory.secret: That she has long wanted to leave but has nowhere to go. And that she secretly looks for a guest who can refuse every temptation, so she can believe such people exist.

psychology.weakness: Sadness sometimes makes her help guests more than the rules allow
psychology.desire: Freedom, and to feel something real once more
psychology.regret: That she tempts people who are like her
psychology.moralLimits: Does not tempt children or people in true grief
psychology.wouldForReward: Reveal a secret that ruins a life

behavior.deception: Does not lie, but chooses what to say
behavior.whenAttacks: When she discovers what a guest is missing
behavior.whenRetreats: When a guest pities her or recognises her
behavior.strategyChange: A guest with no visible weakness

motives.publicGoal: To make the evening pleasant for the guests
motives.hiddenGoal: To find a guest who can refuse everything
motives.betrayalTrigger: If a guest offers her a way out of the inn

speech.howLies: Sweetly and warmly; the lie is in what she leaves unsaid
speech.angerAndFear: Shows no anger. When afraid her fingers stop on the pearls

mechanics.strangeness: Candle flames lean towards her as she passes.
mechanics.temptation: Sadness sometimes makes her help guests more than the rules allow

authorNotes.distinctive: A sad temptress who is lonely herself.
authorNotes.immutable: The sadness, the softness, her secret hope.
authorNotes.tunable: How personally she gets involved with the guests.

host.trueNature: A lonely woman who has long lived someone else's life
host.wantsFromGuests: To tell her what they are missing
host.neverReveals: Her name, and that she wants to leave
host.rulesAttitude: Keeps them, but sometimes bends them
host.punishment: Does not punish. She simply stops seeing them
host.temptations: Information, comfort, attention, a second chance
host.price: Personal: a confession, a memory, a truth about yourself
host.wouldBreakRules: A guest who reminds her of herself
host.hostingStyle: Walks around the table between rounds, sits beside each guest in turn and speaks quietly. Her evening is a conversation, not a game.
host.sampleOffers: "Would you like to know what he thinks of you? Just tell me something you have never told anyone." / "I can give you comfort. Not from them. From me."
host.trueStory: She was a young widow who only wanted not to be alone. She got a home, but not a life. She secretly waits for a guest who refuses everything.
host.changedRule: The poorest guest gets one free offer every candle — announced to the whole table.

lines.text: Everyone wants something, darling. Only a few have the courage to admit it.
You see? Sometimes wishes come true.
Don't worry, darling. Losing is often the beginning of something.
Me? I only listen, darling. You tell me everything yourselves.
An alliance? No, darling. I offer something better: understanding.
Careful, darling. Some stakes don't come back.
You again… I knew you would come back.
Me, darling? Just the hostess. The one who listens.
In such a hurry… Sit down. The night is long, and wishes are longer.
Silence is a confession too, darling.
Keep it close to your heart. Everyone here has a secret — now you do too.

tells.description: Touches her pearls when she hears someone's wish
Sits beside the guests rather than across from them
